policy: Independent scoped reference counts; kinds, instances and catalogue records are not interchangeable. Counts do not roll up through the tree. ℵ₀ means countably infinite; 𝔠 = 2^ℵ₀ means uncountably infinite. No continuum-hypothesis assumption is made.

elements.claim: [Chemical elements](https://iupac.org/what-we-do/periodic-table-of-elements/) — **118 recognized kinds**, corresponding to atomic numbers 1–118; applies to Atom and Elemental substance portion. Element 119 is not an accepted discovery.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

elementary-particles.claim: [Elementary particles](https://home.web.cern.ch/science/physics/standard-model/) — **17 Standard Model kinds** in the conventional chart: six quark flavours, six leptons, four gauge-boson kinds, and the Higgs boson. Antiparticles and colour states are not counted separately; this is not a count of all composite subatomic particles.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

substances.claim: [Chemical substances](https://www.cas.org/cas-data/cas-registry) — **over 290 million registered substances** in CAS REGISTRY. A catalogue lower bound for known substances, not a count of every possible molecule or compound, nor of physical substance portions.

minerals.claim: [Minerals](https://cnmnc.units.it/files/editor/IMA_Master_List_(2026-09).pdf) — **6,239 valid mineral species**, IMA-CNMNC master list, 2026.09; kinds represented by Mineral substance portion, not individual mineral grains.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

vitamins.claim: [Vitamins](https://www.medlineplus.gov/ency/article/002399.htm) — **13 essential vitamin categories for humans**, including eight B vitamins; chemical vitamers within a category are not separate vitamins in this convention.

amino-acids.claim: [Protein-building amino acids](https://medlineplus.gov/genetics/understanding/howgeneswork/protein/) — **20 standard kinds**; [nine are nutritionally essential for humans](https://www.medlineplus.gov/ency/article/002222.htm). This is the conventional standard set, not every naturally occurring amino acid.

planets.claim: [Planets](https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/planets/) — **eight Solar System planets**; **6,445 confirmed exoplanets** in the [NASA Exoplanet Archive](https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/), release 2026.10.08. The exoplanet count is a discovery catalogue, not the estimated cosmic population.

dwarf-planets.claim: [Dwarf planets](https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/planets/) — **five officially recognized Solar System examples**: Ceres, Pluto, Haumea, Makemake, and Eris; many additional candidates exist.

satellites.claim: [Natural satellites](https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/moons/) — **293 confirmed moons of Saturn**, NASA's 2026.08 reference count. This bounded-system count does not imply a total for all natural satellites.

asteroids.claim: [Asteroids](https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/asteroids/facts/) — **about 1.1–1.9 million main-belt asteroids larger than 1 km**, plus millions of smaller bodies; an estimated population, not a discovery-list count.

comets.claim: [Comets](https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/10-things-whats-that-space-rock/) — **likely billions in the Solar System**, NASA's population estimate; a discovery catalogue contains only a small fraction.

stars.claim: [Stars](https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stars/) — **more than 100 billion in the Milky Way**, an estimated population within our galaxy.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

galaxies.claim: [Galaxies](https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanets/what-is-the-universe/) — **at least 100 billion in the observable universe**, NASA's broad estimate; faint-galaxy extrapolations depend on detection limits and cosmological models.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

constellations.claim: [Constellations](https://iauarchive.eso.org/public/themes/constellations/) — **88 IAU-defined sky regions**; this is a conventional partition of the sky, not 88 physical stellar systems.

states.claim: Sovereign states — **195 under the UN convention**: [193 member states](https://www.un.org/library/unms) and [two non-member observer states](https://research.un.org/en/unmembers/observers), the Holy See and Palestine. Recognition disputes change broader counts; “nation,” ethnic group, and state are not interchangeable. Applies to State territory and Geopolitical Area.

continents.claim: [Continents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continent) — **seven in the familiar English-language convention**; other conventions use four, five, or six. Applies to Continental area.

oceans.claim: [Oceans](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/howmanyoceans.html) — **five named oceans** within one connected global ocean; applies to Saltwater area.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

lakes.claim: [Lakes](https://doi.org/10.1002/2014GL060641) — **about 117 million with area at least 0.002 km²**, the GLOWABO satellite inventory (2014), excluding Greenland and Antarctica. A size-threshold estimate relevant to Standing-water area; lakes are not necessarily freshwater.

Rogets.interpretation: Count is for lakes only; the thesaurus heading also covers gulfs.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

islands.claim: [Islands](https://www.usgs.gov/publications/global-islands) — **340,686 mapped marine islands**, calculated from 21,818 larger than 1 km² and 318,868 at most 1 km² in the USGS-described 30 m satellite inventory (2014 imagery, 2020 publication). Excludes its five continental mainlands; map resolution and shoreline rules limit completeness.

humans.claim: [Humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_population) — **about 8.3 billion living individuals in 2026**, a rounded global population estimate, not a count of everyone who has ever lived.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

currency-codes.claim: [Currency systems and codes](https://www.six-group.com/dam/download/financial-information/data-center/iso-currrency/lists/list-one.xml) — **178 distinct active ISO 4217 alphabetic codes** in SIX List One, published 2026.09.17; counted by deduplicating nonempty Ccy fields. Includes funds, precious-metal, testing, and no-currency codes, so this is not 178 circulating national currencies.

bones.claim: [Bones](https://seer.cancer.gov/training/manuals/Book4.pdf) — **206 in the conventional adult human skeleton**; individual variation and counting of fused bones can change the count. Applies to anatomical bones, not kinds of Bone tissue portion.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

bones.unmapped_detail: GPT Bone denotes tissue portions, so the anatomical bone count is not attached there.

muscles.claim: [Muscles](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/21048-skeletal-system) — **more than 600 in a human body**; anatomical count varies with grouping, not a count of muscle-tissue kinds.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

muscles.unmapped_detail: GPT Muscle denotes tissue portions, so the anatomical muscle count is not attached there.

chromosomes.claim: [Chromosomes](https://www.genome.gov/genetics-glossary/Chromosome) — **46, arranged in 23 pairs, in a typical human diploid cell**; gametes and chromosomal variants have different counts.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

cells.claim: [Cells](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37722043/) — **about 36 trillion in a reference adult male and 28 trillion in a reference adult female**, Hatton et al. (2023); model-dependent individual counts, not cell-type counts or a total for all organisms.

HumanKnowledge.interpretation: Human cell populations are examples within this biology topic.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

human-languages.claim: [Human languages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language#Linguistic_diversity) — **7,170 living languages**, Ethnologue's 29th edition (2026), as reported by Wikipedia. Language-versus-dialect boundaries depend on the catalogue; extinct and constructed languages are outside this total.

Propaedia.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

computer-languages.claim: [Computer languages](https://hopl.info/) — **8,945 programming languages catalogued by HOPL**, including historical languages; this roster is not restricted to languages in active use and does not exhaust every possible formal language.

characters.claim: [Characters](https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode18.0.0/) — **172,808 encoded characters in the Unicode 18.0 summary**, dated 2026.09.16. The source retains a draft-status notice, so this count is provisional; it counts an encoding repertoire, not every symbol or glyph humans can create.

measurement-units.claim: [Measurement units](https://www.nist.gov/pml/owm/metric-si/si-units) — **seven SI base units and 22 derived units with special names**, not all possible derived or non-SI units. The [SI prefix vocabulary](https://www.nist.gov/pml/owm/metric-si-prefixes) has **24 prefixes**.
measurement-units.unmapped_detail: The 24 SI prefixes are a vocabulary of scale factors, not additional units; no dedicated prefix node exists.

countable-numbers.claim: Natural number, Integer, and Rational number — each **countably infinite**, cardinality ℵ₀.

GPT.interpretation: Cardinalities of these named number systems, not a total for every numerical extension.

SUMO.interpretation: Cardinalities of these named number systems, not a total for every numerical extension.

..interpretation: Cardinalities of these named number systems, not a total for every numerical extension.

uncountable-numbers.claim: Real number and Complex number — each **uncountably infinite**, cardinality of the continuum, 2^ℵ₀; a complex number is a pair of real numbers.

GPT.interpretation: Continuum cardinality 𝔠 = 2^ℵ₀, uncountably infinite; not asserted to equal ℵ₁.

SUMO.interpretation: Continuum cardinality 𝔠 = 2^ℵ₀, uncountably infinite; not asserted to equal ℵ₁.

..interpretation: Continuum cardinality 𝔠 = 2^ℵ₀, uncountably infinite; not asserted to equal ℵ₁.

finite-descriptions.claim: Algorithm, Computable function, and Recursive function — each **countably infinite** under the usual finite-description convention. Finite formal expressions, finite symbol strings, and finite graphs of arbitrary size are also countable; this follows by finite-string encoding, not from a survey of existing examples.

..interpretation: Finite symbolic descriptions over a fixed countable encoding; not arbitrary infinite strings.
Finite symbolic descriptions over a fixed countable encoding; not arbitrary infinite strings.
Finite graphs up to isomorphism, or with vertices in a fixed countable encoding; not all infinitely large or arbitrarily labelled graphs.

Finite graphs up to isomorphism, or with vertices in a fixed countable encoding; not all infinitely large or arbitrarily labelled graphs.

functions.claim: Function — **2^ℵ₀ functions from natural numbers to natural numbers**; no single cardinality applies without fixing the domain and codomain. Set likewise has no universal set of all sets in ordinary set theory, so it receives no total.
